subject: Post-demo: SDK auth failures & routing fallback plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgefin.com>
Cc: Alex Jones <alex.jones@edgefin.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SDK auth failures & routing fallback plan

Thanks again for the call earlier — great walkthrough. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock your integration:

- Issue observed: intermittent 5xx errors when the SDK exchanges the session token for an active model route (happens ~5–10% of requests during load tests).
- Hypothesis: the auth exchange times out under connection bursts; routing policy falls back to default and hits a model variant with incompatible input shape, generating 502/500.

Proposed next actions:
1) Send us the SDK debug trace you captured (you mentioned sdk_trace_20260614.log).
2) We'll reproduce on our staging with your request payload and the same routing policy.
3) If reproduced, SE will propose a prod-safe mitigation (timeout tuning + temporary routing rule to force stable model variant).

Can you confirm you can share the trace and the payload? I'll loop in Monica (SE) to get a repro and a short-term mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Rishi
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal_onepager.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: SDK auth failures & routing fallback plan

Looping you in — customer (EdgeFin) provided traces and payloads showing intermittent 5xxs during session token exchange. Key lines in trace show repeated POST /v1/sessions -> 502 from routing service.

Customer environment: Java SDK v1.3.2, default timeouts (connect 2s/read 10s), ~200 concurrent sessions during ramp.

Can you take a look for repro steps and whether this sounds like timeout vs routing mismatch? If we can reproduce, let's suggest a short-term policy change to route them to the stable small-llama variant for 100% of traffic.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgefin.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: SDK auth failures & routing fallback plan

Thanks for the ping — I'll own repro. Quick notes from preliminary look:

- The trace shows repeated HTTP 502/503 at the auth handoff step (token -> route lookup). That suggests either a transient gateway timeout or the route-caching layer returning a nil mapping and the router hitting a default backend that rejects the payload.
- Two immediate checks for the customer to run on their side:
  1) Increase SDK connect/read timeouts to connect=5s, read=20s and retry the load test; this will tell us if it's a timing sensitivity.
  2) Turn on SDK debug header X-RI-Debug: true and re-run a failing request to capture full upstream headers (we need the routing route-id).

Repro plan (our staging):
- Use provided edgefin_request_payload.json and sdk_trace to replay at 250 concurrent sessions for 2 minutes.
- If we observe identical 5xx, we'll toggle routing: set a canary policy for EdgeFin's account to always pick the small-llama-stable variant for 100% of their traffic for 10 minutes and re-run.

I'll post results here and include a short mitigation playbook (cURL toggles, console steps) if reproduced.

-Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: repro_steps.md (inline)

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgefin.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK auth failures & routing fallback plan

Thanks Monica — ran quick test with increased timeouts (connect=5s/read=20s). Error rate dropped from ~12% to ~2%, so timeout sensitivity definitely a factor. I also enabled X-RI-Debug and attached the header dump (see rdw_auth_debug.png). I still see occasional 502s with a route-id that looks like "rt-unstable-34".

If switching the route to small-llama-stable reduces errors to near-zero, that's a good temporary workaround for us while we tune routing.

-Sanjay

Attachment: rdw_auth_debug.png

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgefin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK auth failures & routing fallback plan

Great — thanks for the quick repro, Sanjay. Based on this:

- Short-term mitigation: We'll apply a per-account routing override to force EdgeFin to the small-llama-stable variant for the next 2 hours during your ramp window. This is reversible and low-risk.
- Medium-term: We'll audit the router's cache invalidation and the route-selection fallback to ensure null mappings are handled without hitting an incompatible backend.

Steps I'll take now:
1) Schedule the canary override for today at 16:00 UTC for 2 hours; I'll confirm once it's active and provide console toggles + rollback steps.
2) Run the staging replay at 250 concurrent sessions after override and share pass/fail numbers.
3) Create a follow-up ticket for infra to trace route-cache eviction edge cases (will include the route-id traces you provided).

Expect a confirmation within 30 minutes.

-Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: console_override_instructions.txt
